title: Which means of travel covers one, three and five digit distances?
description: Farhan reads a chart of how far each means of travel goes in one hour. The video counts the digits of each distance to match the question.
teaching_notes: One idea: count the digits of the number to know its size. Watch for children who call twelve a one digit number because it is small.

source: Which means of travel covers a 1-digit, a 3-digit and a 5-di
video_script.why: The child can read big numbers but has not yet used the number of digits to sort the distances people travel in an hour.
video_script.substitution: Read each distance on the chart, count its digits, and match the count to the question.
video_script.anchor: Farhan's hourly distance chart on the classroom wall in Lucknow
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu calls twelve a one digit number because it is small. Twelve is written with a one and a two, so it has two digits.
video_script.payoff_line: on foot, by aircraft and by spacecraft

final_answer.value: On foot, by aircraft and by spacecraft
final_answer.spoken: on foot, by aircraft and by spacecraft

hold_back: On foot, by aircraft and by spacecraft
never_show: the cycle marked as a one digit means
maths_rules: chart, kilometres in one hour: on foot 3 to 5; cycle 12 to 20; motorbike 40 to 60; aircraft 750 to 920; spacecraft at least 28,000
1 digit: below 10, so 3, 4 and 5 have 1 digit; on foot
3 digits: 100 to 999, so 750 and 920 have 3 digits; aircraft
5 digits: 10,000 to 99,999, so 28,000 has 5 digits (2, 8, 0, 0, 0); spacecraft
slip: 12 is small but has 2 digits, so the cycle is a 2 digit means
your turn: a train going 110 km in an hour; 110 has 3 digits; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: count the digits. Wrong idea: small means one digit. The chart stays on the stage; each row lights when it is tested.

narration: <bookmark mark='m27'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m28'/>Farhan reads a chart on the wall of his classroom in Lucknow.
<bookmark mark='m29'/>It tells how far each means of travel goes in one hour.
<bookmark mark='m30'/>Think of the kilometres covered in one hour.
<bookmark mark='m31'/>Which means of travel covers a one digit, a three digit and a five digit number?

narration: <bookmark mark='m33'/>Here is the chart, one row at a time.
<bookmark mark='m34'/>On foot, a person goes three to five kilometres in an hour.
<bookmark mark='m35'/>A cycle goes twelve to twenty kilometres, and a motorbike goes forty to sixty.
<bookmark mark='m36'/>An aircraft goes seven hundred and fifty to nine hundred and twenty kilometres.
<bookmark mark='m37'/>A spacecraft goes at least twenty eight thousand kilometres in an hour.

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='m38'/>A cycle goes twelve kilometres, and twelve is small, so it is a one digit number.
<bookmark mark='m39'/>Small does not mean one digit.
<bookmark mark='m40'/>Count the digits in twelve. There is a one and a two.
<bookmark mark='m41'/>Twelve has two digits.

narration: <bookmark mark='m42'/>A one digit number is less than ten.
<bookmark mark='m43'/>Three, four and five all have one digit, so walking on foot fits.
<bookmark mark='m44'/>A three digit number is from one hundred to nine hundred and ninety nine.
<bookmark mark='m45'/>Seven hundred and fifty and nine hundred and twenty both have three digits, so the aircraft fits.

narration: <bookmark mark='m46'/>A five digit number is ten thousand or more.
<bookmark mark='m47'/>Twenty eight thousand has a two, an eight and three zeros, which is five digits.
<bookmark mark='m48'/>A spacecraft fits.
<bookmark mark='m49'/>The answer is on foot, by aircraft and by spacecraft.
